title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes the char-3 half of Proposition 7.2(II). The proposition says the ring of modular forms (Katz–Deligne sense: rules on Weierstrass curves with a chosen invariant differential, of fixed weight) over F_3 is F_3[b_2, Δ], with c_4 = b_2^2 and c_6 = -b_2^3.

Argument, step by step:
1. In characteristic 3, b_2 is itself a modular form of weight 2. It is the Hasse invariant: it vanishes exactly on supersingular curves, which in char 3 are those with j = 0.
2. First restrict to curves with c_4 = b_2^2 invertible, i.e. j ≠ 0. After completing the square and translating x, such a curve can be written y^2 = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_6. Killing a_4 is possible because b_2 = a_2 is invertible; this is the remark 'd_6 = 0 équivaut à a_4 = 0' on the previous page.
3. On these normal forms the residual automorphism group is small. A form of weight k is then an isobaric expression in a_2 = b_2 and a_6, with b_2 inverted.
4. Here Δ = -b_2^2 b_8 = -b_2^3 a_6, so a_6 = -Δ/b_2^3. Hence every such form can be written b_2^{-n} P(b_2, Δ) with P isobaric.
5. Such a form extends over the supersingular locus j = 0 (b_2 = 0, Δ invertible) iff the expression is actually a polynomial in b_2 and Δ.
6. Hence the ring is F_3[b_2, Δ].

The whole argument mirrors the char-2 case on the previous page, which uses a_1 (the char-2 Hasse invariant) and the normal form y^2 + a_1 xy = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_6.

The proposition serves the previous page's claim. Since the ring structure mod 2 and mod 3 is known, a polynomial in c_4, c_6, Δ that vanishes as a form mod 2 (resp. 3) is divisible by c_4^3 - c_6^2 - 1728Δ, which reduces to c_4^3 - c_6^2. This feeds the computation of the ring of modular forms over Z.

The text is Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire (d'après J. Tate)', published in Modular Functions of One Variable IV, LNM 476 (1975), §7. This is a typescript copy in Grothendieck's files, not Grothendieck's own mathematics.
errors: No mathematical errors. The step 'extends over j = 0 iff polynomial' implicitly uses normality/codimension-one reasoning: Δ is invertible, so the only possible pole is along b_2 = 0. It also uses the fact that the j = 0 curves form a divisor where b_2 vanishes to order one. Both points are standard but are only sketched here.

ideas.what: Ring of mod-3 modular forms is F_3[b_2, Δ], with b_2 the Hasse invariant (c_4 = b_2^2, c_6 = -b_2^3); mod 2 analogue F_2[a_1, Δ]
ideas.modern_name: Structure of the ring of mod p modular forms of level 1 for p = 2, 3; Hasse invariant
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Formulaire, Antwerp IV, LNM 476, 1975), after Tate; cf. Swinnerton-Dyer, Serre, Katz for p ≥ 5
ideas.where_published: Deligne, 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire d'après J. Tate', LNM 476 (1975), Prop. 7.2

ideas.what: Normal form y^2 = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_6 for ordinary curves in char 3, and expressing forms as b_2^{-n}P(b_2, Δ) with extension criterion over j = 0
ideas.modern_name: Extension of modular forms across the supersingular locus
